page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration supplies 8 dedicated virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 64.0 GB of system memory. This yields a memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 vector instructions and AES encryption acceleration. The instance provides 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, while containing no bundled local NVMe storage or attached GPU accelerators.

Benchmark testing indicates modest overall compute performance paired with solid memory throughput for standard operations. Multi-threaded CPU execution recorded a stress-ng score of 5,868.66 and a PassMark CPU score of 7,037.75, positioning processing capabilities in the lower-to-middle tier. Uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth reached 39.75 GB/sec and 36.51 GB/sec respectively. Specialized tasks like single-threaded compression demonstrate lower throughput, but key-value storage performance remains solid, as shown by Redis SET execution reaching 5.94 million operations per second.

Given the high 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and baseline network capacity, the ecs.se1.2xlarge is suited for in-memory caching, relational database buffers, key-value stores, and light data analytics requiring substantial memory without high single-thread compute demands. Workloads heavily reliant on sequential local disk IOPS or intensive matrix operations will require network-attached storage or higher-tier compute architectures.
